'''Mahmud Karimov''' (18 October 1948; [[Yerevan]], [[Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic|Armenian SSR]] - 10 February 2013; [[Istanbul]], Turkey) was an [[Azerbaijanis|Azerbaijani]] physicist, Doctor of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, Professor, President of the [[Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan.]]

== Life ==
Mahmud Karimov was born in [[Yerevan]] and graduated from the physics faculty of [[Baku State University|Azerbaijan State University]].{{cn|date=July 2025}}

Karimov's main research was related to radiation physics, informatics and physics of dielectrics. He also conducted scientific research in the fields of [[radioecology]] and radiation materials science. He headed the Radiation Research Sector for a long time and, in 2001, was elected a full member of the Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences. Karimov collaborated with the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] and worked on several projects related to radiation research. He was also a member of the commissions of [[Commonwealth of Independent States|CIS]] countries and Turkic countries on peaceful use of atomic energy. He was the president of ANAS from 2001 to 2013.<ref>{{cite web
 |url         = https://science.gov.az/az/forms/byivshie-prezidentyi/175
 |title       = Kərimov Mahmud Kərim oğlu
 |author      = [[Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences|ANAS]]
 |date        = 2013
 |work        = 
 |publisher   = science.gov.az
 |accessdate  = 2 July 2023
 |language    = 
}}</ref>

Karimov was the author of more than 200 articles and the owner of numerous patents. He worked as the president of the National Academy of Sciences, the chairman of the Republican Council for the Organization and Coordination of Scientific Research.<ref>{{cite web
 |url         = https://apa.az/az/news/287996
 |title       = Azərbaycan prezidenti və bir qrup dövlət və elm xadimi akademik Mahmud Kərimovun vəfatı ilə əlaqədar nekroloq imzalayıblar
 |author      = 
 |date        = 10 February 2010
 |work        = 
 |publisher   = apa.az
 |accessdate  = 2 July 2023
 |language    = 
}}</ref>

Mahmud Kerimov had two children named Sabina and Farid. He died on February 10, 2013, from a heart failure attack in one of the clinics in Istanbul, where he was urgently delivered by a special flight from Baku for emergency medical care. He was buried in the [[Alley of Honor|First Alley of Honor]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url         = https://apa.az/az/news/287993
 |title       = Azərbaycan Milli Elmlər Akademiyasının prezidenti Mahmud Kərimov dünyasını dəyişib
 |author      = 
 |date        = 10 February 2013
 |work        = 
 |publisher   = apa.az
 |accessdate  = 2 July 2023
 |language    = 
}}</ref>
